texts.facts: "The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner" 1. In this case, a detailed accident report was filed by police in terms of provisions of Motor Vehicle Act, same is treated as Claim Petition in view of the provisions contained in such Act. 2. Brief facts of the case as per the investigation by the Police officials concerned are that on 15.07.2019, concerned police official received GD no. 3A regarding MLC of injured Rajbir and reached AIIMS Trauma Centre where he collected the MLC of Rajbir Singh vs . Shariq Parvez & Ors. on 12 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132260473/ 1 injured. Further, on 22.06.2019, ASI recorded the statement of injured wherein he stated that on 14.07.2019, he along with his brother Satyavir going to their house on foot by Taimur Nagar and at about 10.00 PM, when they reached near Gurudwara, Taimur Nagar, R-1/ driver of offending vehicle drove his car from back side and ran over his right leg. He suffered injuries as a result thereof. The driver of offending vehicle came to him at the spot of accident and claimant noted the vehicle number of offending vehicle as DL 6CR 8052 Baleno Car and the name of the R-1. Such driver even offered medical treatment of the injured / claimant. Brother of the claimant took the claimant to AIIMS Trauma Center and they did not told about such accident at that time. But later on on the complaint of claimant, present FIR was registered u/s 279, 338 IPC based on the MLC and the statement of claimant. 3. Further after investigation, chargesheet u/s 279/338 was filed. Further more, present DAR is also filed by the concerned police official. 4. Further as per record R-1/ driver cum owner appeared initially but he did not file any reply and later on stopped appearing. MACT No.:687/19 Rajbir Singh Vs. Shariq Parvez & Anr. Page No. 2 of 22 5 . But, as a reply is filed by insurance company/R-3. Insurance of the offending vehicle with R3 is not denied. But it is stated that such insurance liability of R-3is subject to compliance of terms and condition of insurance policy, including holding of valid driving license, permit and fitness certificate. It is further claimed that accident took place due to so negligence of petitioner only. Further, it is claimed that delay of 9 days in registration of FIR. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by Ld. Predecessor of this Tribunal on 23.01.2020: i). OPP. ii). Relief. 7. As per record, claimant examined himself in chief as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. He relied upon various documents including discharge summary and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/7 relating to his identity and medical treatment and bills. 8. He was cross-examined by learned counsel for insurance company. Rajbir Singh vs . Shariq Parvez & Ors. on 12 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/132260473/ 2 9. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioners. 10. Further, as per record, none of the respondent led any evidence. 11. Further, as per record, a medical physical disability certificate, issued by Pt. Madan Mohan Malviya hospital, New Delhi dated MACT No.:687/19 Rajbir Singh Vs. Shariq Parvez & Anr. Page No. 3 of 22 12.04.2022 noting the disability of the present injured/claimant as 17% regarding right lower limb.

The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 29.
